slides.title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MORTAL AGENT LEARNS LINGUISTIC AGENCY
slides.highlight: This research introduces an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) that learns how linguistic choices affect a partner's willingness to protect its viability, providing insights into embodied social robots and human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: An Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) learns linguistic affordances by linking social expressions to bodily survival.
card.key_idea: Mortality-Grounded Linguistic Reinforcement Learning (MGL-RL) couples a Bayesian partner-response model with a homeostatic body, where linguistic choices are valued by their effect on remaining useful life.
card.evaluation: Controlled experiments using a cohort of EMAs across 60 encounters, employing matched counterfactual continuations and ablations to trace causal contributions of embodiment and precariousness.
card.limitation: The agent's linguistic capacity is limited to a fixed action repertoire rendered into text, rather than open-ended natural language generation.

slides.title: C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees
slides.tldr: CAUSAL REASONING FOR SENTIMENT SHIFTS IN SOCIAL MEDIA
slides.highlight: This work introduces C$^{3}$T, a model for predicting sentiment shifts and causal attribution in conversation trees, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: C³T uses counterfactual causal reasoning to attribute sentiment shifts to specific discourse moves in conversation trees.
card.key_idea: A thread-structured Transformer that jointly predicts sentiment and shifts, utilizes intervention embeddings for counterfactual queries, and employs an IRM-style penalty for event-level invariance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on rumor datasets against neural and LLM baselines using macro-F1 and Top-1 accuracy; C³T showed superior event-OOD robustness and attribution.
card.limitation: Cross-thread spillovers are treated as a limitation, and causal estimates are model-based and conditional on measured context.

slides.title: Towards a Foundational Ontology for Identifying and Resolving Contradictions in Dialogue-based Human-Robot Interactions
slides.tldr: ONTOLOGY FOR RESOLVING HRI DIALOGUE CONTRADICTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a foundational ontology (ATFOt) to represent and resolve contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot interactions, supporting the RwB goal of improving embodied social robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A foundational ontology to formally represent and resolve contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot and human-agent interactions.
card.key_idea: Utilizes METHONTOLOGY and Activity Theory to define contradictions (errors, conflicts, knowledge issues) via Set Theory, First Order Logic, and a four-level abstraction hierarchy.
card.evaluation: Preliminary results include natural language and logic definitions; full evaluation via coverage and competency questions is currently ongoing using Protege.
card.limitation: The work is currently in the preliminary/ongoing stage, with full implementation and qualitative validation not yet completed.

slides.title: Humanoid bartender debuts in Hong Kong’s nightlife hub
slides.highlight: The debut of a humanoid bartender in Hong Kong provides a real-world example of embodied social robots interacting with humans in a public setting, relevant to RwB.

slides.title: How Much Can AI Understand? Toward AI-Assisted Sensemaking of Collaborative Discussion in Groups with Shared History
slides.highlight: This work proposes a model for AI-assisted sensemaking that captures group norms, participants, and social context, aligning with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Proposes an AI model for sensemaking in group discussions by incorporating social context and shared history.
card.key_idea: An AI-assisted sensemaking model that extracts and connects arguments, community norms, and participant contexts, operating across a spectrum of low-to-high system interpretive work.
card.evaluation: Based on two studies of experienced Wikipedia editors' cognitive processes and a web-based LLM-assisted prototype; results are not quantitatively detailed.
card.limitation: High system interpretive work risks dehumanizing participants, erasing minority opinions, and creating false consensus if the AI lacks social intelligibility.

slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich human-robot interaction in assistive care, emphasizing the need for physics-aware screening beyond simple task success. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion does not imply physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated against real manikin force-indentation measurements with a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol and physics-aware scoring.
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs/method) using task success, peak force, and joint-limit margins.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue and reuses forearm calibration for the upper arm.

slides.title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous and Field-Induced Mechanisms of Collective Behavior in One Dimension
slides.tldr: HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION PROVES STATISTICAL PHYSICS THEOREM
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how human-AI collaboration can generate scientific hypotheses outside a human's active hypothesis space to prove theorems on collective behavior. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on the impact of human-AI societies and the use of AI agents for modeling and discovery.

card.one_liner: A human-AI collaboration proves a theorem mapping 1D range-two spin chains to simpler range-one chains.
card.key_idea: A recursive Householder moving-frame transformation maps O(n) and Potts open chains with arbitrary inhomogeneous interactions to range-one chains with axial potentials, regardless of system size.
card.evaluation: The theorem was validated by recovering known Ising/XY results and solving the previously unsolved J1-J2 Potts open chain in closed form.
card.limitation: The mapping is specifically proven for open boundary conditions (OBC) rather than periodic systems.

slides.title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
slides.highlight: TEIDAN provides a multimodal corpus of triadic conversations that supports research on addressee recognition and turn-taking, aligning with HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: TEIDAN is a multilingual multimodal corpus of spontaneous three-party face-to-face discussions in Japanese and English.
card.key_idea: The corpus uses pin microphones, microphone arrays, and cameras to record triadic interactions, providing IPU-based transcripts for cross-linguistic analysis of turn-taking and multimodal grounding.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via descriptive quantitative statistics (IPU/pseudo-turn counts) and qualitative sequential analysis of turn construction across 69 sessions.
card.limitation: Cross-linguistic comparisons are confounded by participant relationships: Japanese speakers were acquainted colleagues, while English speakers were strangers.

slides.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
slides.tldr: ASR ERRORS INCREASE EMBODIED AI SAFETY RISKS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how automatic speech recognition errors can bypass model refusal behaviors and lead to the execution of harmful instructions, which is critical for the safety of social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: ASR errors in voice-controlled embodied AI can bypass safety filters and trigger unsafe executable behaviors.
card.key_idea: A framework simulating five ASR error types (e.g., acoustic substitution, noise) was integrated with POEX and SafeAgentBench to test model refusal and planning robustness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Qwen2.5-7B, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4.1-mini using Acceptance Rate and Success Rate; results show ASR errors increase safety flips and decrease planning success.
card.limitation: Automatic ASR correction is not always effective, particularly when input semantics are heavily damaged by severe noise.

slides.title: Behavior--Realization Separation for Constrained Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: SEPARATING BEHAVIOR SPECIFICATION FROM CONSTRAINED REALIZATION IN pHRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a layered architecture that separates desired behavior from constrained realization, improving precision and torque feasibility in physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A control architecture separating desired interaction behavior from physical robot realization to improve constraint handling.
card.key_idea: A behavior layer provides desired acceleration via an affine interface; a predictive QP realization layer converts this into feasible robot commands while reporting a decomposed realization residual.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via planar simulations and a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo, comparing predictive realization against reactive clipping for workspace and torque constraints.
card.limitation: The predictive QP implementation is validated only for memoryless affine behaviors; nonlinear or stateful specifications may require different prediction machinery.

slides.title: Humanoid Robots Are Fashion’s Future Clients. Hansae Is Getting Ready to Dress Them
slides.highlight: Hansae is preparing to create clothing for humanoid robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Remote Human and Robot Interaction for Greenhouse Gardening Using Virtual Reality
slides.highlight: This research explores VR-based remote human-robot interaction for plant inspection, providing insights into how sensory occlusion affects task success, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: VR-based robot teleoperation for greenhouse gardening is limited by plant canopy occlusion rather than operator skill.
card.key_idea: An unmanned ground vehicle with a robotic manipulator and VR interface used for remote leaf inspection and soil moisture assessment via kinematic control.
card.evaluation: Fourteen plants tested across two experiments; measured cycle times, disease detection accuracy (up to 88%), and soil moisture assessment success (up to 64.3%).
card.limitation: Dense, compound plant canopies cause camera occlusion, significantly reducing sensing reliability regardless of operator experience.

slides.title: Fobi AI Launches AgenticBrain
slides.highlight: The launch of AgenticBrain introduces conversational agentic AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and human-AI team states.

slides.title: Social bots weaken activist cohesion
slides.highlight: This research examines how bot exposure disrupts human network ties and collective action, providing insights into social perception and group dynamics relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Social bot exposure during protest peaks erodes the human network cohesion necessary to sustain collective action.
card.key_idea: Using 2020 BLM retweet networks, the authors measured triadic closure in ego networks and edge density in communities to link bot exposure to subsequent human tie decay.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via longitudinal Twitter data (pre, during, and post-peak) using OLS regressions and GPT-3.5 for stance classification; results were robust across bot-probability thresholds.
card.limitation: The study focuses on a specific event (2020 BLM protests), which may limit generalizability to other movements or platforms.
